Add persistent server mode: Unix socket PTY relay

Server owns PTY child processes so agents survive TUI disconnects.
TUI connects via Unix socket (~/.aimux/aimux.sock) to relay I/O.
Without server, everything works exactly as before (direct PTY mode).

- Server: spawn/write/resize/screen/kill/list protocol over socket
- ServerClient + ServerSession: client-side socket proxy matching PtySession interface
- Multiplexer: auto-connects to server on startup, reconnects to live sessions
- TUI exit disconnects from server (agents keep running), server stop saves state
- Dashboard: shows "● server" in header, green ⬡ on server-backed sessions
- Tray: start/stop server controls, server ownership indicators per agent

Add server mode: TerminalIO abstraction + Unix socket daemon

Major refactor: abstracted all terminal I/O behind a TerminalIO
interface so the multiplexer can run in direct mode (current behavior)
or server mode (output over Unix socket to a thin client).

TerminalIO abstraction (terminal-io.ts):
- TerminalIO interface for write, dimensions, input, resize, raw mode
- DirectTerminalIO: wraps process.stdin/stdout (current behavior)
- RemoteTerminalIO: backed by Unix socket with length-prefixed protocol

Server mode (server.ts):
- `aimux server start` — spawns background daemon, Unix socket at
  ~/.aimux/aimux.sock, PID file at ~/.aimux/aimux.pid
- `aimux server stop` — sends SIGTERM to running server
- `aimux server status` — checks if server is running
- Single client at a time, PTYs survive client disconnect

Client (client.ts):
- `aimux attach` — connects to running server
- Forwards stdin/stdout over protocol, handles resize
- Ctrl+\ to detach (server keeps running)
- Auto-detect: `aimux` attaches if server is running

Multiplexer refactor:
- Replaced all ~60 direct process.stdin/stdout references with this.io.*
- Constructor accepts optional TerminalIO (defaults to DirectTerminalIO)
- Zero process.stdout/stdin references remain in multiplexer.ts
- HotkeyHandler also refactored to use TerminalIO

Fix agent crash on spawn: shell-escape preamble args properly

Root cause: the preamble was wrapped in single quotes for the shell
command, but the worktree preamble contained literal single quotes
(e.g., worktree 'name') which broke the shell quoting. zsh reported
"unmatched '" and exited with code 1.

Fix: added proper shell escaping in pty-session.ts that handles
embedded single quotes using the standard '\'' technique. Also
replaced single quotes with double quotes in the worktree preamble.

Additionally fixed: updateHeartbeat() no longer prunes its own instance
entry (could self-prune if heartbeat was delayed >15s), and added a
safety check in the multiplexer to skip claim detection when previousIds
is empty to prevent false-positive session removal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix cross-instance session visibility and unknown worktree display

Bug: new sessions weren't appearing in other instances' dashboards.
Root cause: updateHeartbeat() was incorrectly filtering new sessions
as "claimed" when the registry already had other sessions registered.

Fix: simplified updateHeartbeat() to just return previousSessionIds
(what the registry had before the write). Claim detection is now
entirely in the multiplexer via confirmedRegistered set — only sessions
that were previously confirmed as registered can be detected as claimed.

Also fixed "unknown (unknown)" worktree labels for offline sessions by
resolving worktree name/branch from the registry on display.

- instance-registry.ts: registration, heartbeat, claim detection (10 tests)

Fixed claim detection: updateHeartbeat() only flags sessions as claimed

Bug 2: Offline sessions in the dashboard now carry backendSessionId so
cross-worktree resume can find the correct backend conversation.

Bug 3: state.json now reads/writes from the main repo's .aimux/ (like
instances.json) so offline agents are visible across worktrees.

Boot to dashboard when another instance takes over the focused agent

session was the focused agent, instance A switches to the dashboard.
The local PTY is killed to avoid two instances talking to the same
backend session.

updateHeartbeat() now returns IDs of sessions that were claimed since
last heartbeat by comparing the registry entry against expected state.

discover each other and show remote agents on the dashboard. Users can
take over agents from other instances via [t] hotkey, which claims the
session and resumes it with --resume. State is merged on exit so cold
starts resume all agents regardless of which instance owned them.

New file: src/instance-registry.ts
Modified: multiplexer.ts, dashboard.ts, hotkeys.ts, config.ts
